MEMORANDUM
TO: William Flynn, Secretary
Executive Office of Community Affairs
FROM: Evelyn F. Murphy, Secretary
Executive Office of Environmental Anfairs
DATE: August 9, 1977
RE: EOEA #01891, Draft Environmental Impact Report Kendall Square Urban Renewal Project, Cambridge
My statement that the above referenced Draft Report adequately and properly complies with General Laws, Chapter 30, Section 62, was made subject to the condition that the comments set forth in this memorandum are considered and fully responded to in the final report.
I. NOISE IMPACT
The Noise Impact Analysis of the proposed Kendall Square Urban Renewal Project is a well researched document. In the study, special considerations are given to the human environment - possible residential or hotel activities within the project and possible noise exposure of pedestrians - and subsequent evaluation of the noise sensitive land uses under the different plans support the decision that Parcels 3 and 4 should be devoted to retail, residential and and hotel buildings. In addition, the elimination of the Kendall Square Rotery and replacement of the existing streets with a new network system are viewed as effective tools for traffic noise control.
The proposed development, however, is situated in an Area which at several locations now exceeds HUD noise standards. The Draft Report reveals that the development in Parcels 3 and 4 are expected to receive "Unacceptable" noise exposure in fringe facing busy streets. (Fig. 11.7.3, in addition, reveals "Normally Unacceptance" noise levels well within these parcels). Further, pedestrians travelling along Main St., Broadway and Western St. would also be exposed to "Unacceptable" noise levels.
